problems.sourceStatement: Obtain a separation between computing the spectral gap of undirected Laplacians to n^{-1} additive error and solving general integer matrices, or show reductions between them.
problems.problem: Complexity of finding $\lambda_2(L)$ to high accuracy
problems.wordDescription:
The spectral gap $\lambda_2(L)$ is the smallest nonzero eigenvalue of the combinatorial Laplacian of a connected weighted graph. Two very different upper bounds are known. Dense Hermitian eigensolvers ignore the graph structure entirely: Sobczyk's deterministic algorithm computes every eigenvalue of an $n\times n$ Hermitian matrix in $O(n^{\omega}\mathcal F(\log(n/\epsilon))+n^2\,\mathrm{polylog}(n/\epsilon))$ bit operations, and the randomized algorithms of Banks, Garza-Vargas, Kulkarni and Srivastava and of Shah run in nearly matrix-multiplication time with $\mathrm{polylog}$ or $\log(1/\epsilon)+O(\log n)$ bits of precision, so $n^{-1}$-accurate $\lambda_2$ costs $\tilde O(n^{\omega})$ bit operations for any $m$. Solver-based methods exploit the structure: Spielman and Teng run inverse power iteration with their nearly-linear-time solver and obtain a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximate Fiedler vector in $O(m\log^{c}m\log(1/p)\log(1/\epsilon)/\epsilon)$ time, and Krylov (Lanczos) methods with a random start reduce the $1/\epsilon$ dependence to $\tilde O(1/\sqrt{\epsilon})$ solves; but the additive target $n^{-1}$ forces relative accuracy $\epsilon=1/(n\lambda_2(L))$, which can be as small as $\Theta(n^{-12})$ for weights up to $n^{10}$, so these routes are only nearly linear when $\lambda_2(L)$ is large.

What is not known is whether Laplacian structure makes $n^{-1}$-additive gap estimation polynomially cheaper than solving a general polynomially conditioned integer system (comparison points $O(n^{\omega})$ dense and $\tilde O(n^{(3\omega-4)/(\omega-1)})$ sparse), or whether a sparsity-preserving reduction in the style of Kyng and Zhang's hardness results for structured linear systems transfers the general-linear-algebra barrier to $\lambda_2(L)$. The only unconditional lower bounds found are in restricted models: Simchowitz, El Alaoui and Recht give gap-dependent matrix-vector query lower bounds, and Braverman, Hazan, Simchowitz and Woodworth show that polynomially accurate largest-eigenvector computation needs $\Theta(d)$ matrix-vector queries, which rules out fast Krylov-type black-box methods but says nothing about bit complexity. No result found through 2026-09-20 gives the requested reduction or separation for unnormalized integer-weighted Laplacians.
problems.mathematicalConditions:
Input: a connected undirected graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $m$ edges and integer weights $w_e\in[1,n^{10}]$, given explicitly, with combinatorial Laplacian $L=D-A$ and eigenvalues $0=\lambda_1(L)<\lambda_2(L)\le\dots\le\lambda_n(L)$. The scale is fixed by $\lambda_2(L)\ge 8/n^2$ (Fiedler's bound for connected graphs with weights at least $1$) and $\lambda_2(L)\le\|L\|\le 2n^{11}$. Task: output $\tilde\lambda$ with $|\tilde\lambda-\lambda_2(L)|\le n^{-1}$, deterministically or with success probability at least $1-1/n$, in the classical high-accuracy regime: cost is measured in bit operations (equivalently word operations on $O(\log n)$-bit words times $\mathrm{polylog}$ factors), and polylogarithmic factors are suppressed. The error is absolute for the unnormalized Laplacian and is equivalent to relative error $\epsilon=1/(n\lambda_2(L))\in[\,n^{-12}/2,\;n/8\,]$; normalized-Laplacian or constant-relative-error variants are different problems. Baselines: (i) structure-oblivious dense eigensolvers, namely Sobczyk (arXiv:2410.21550), which deterministically computes all eigenvalues of a Hermitian $A$ with $\|A\|\le 1$ to additive error $\epsilon$ in $O(n^{\omega}\mathcal F(\log(n/\epsilon))+n^2\,\mathrm{polylog}(n/\epsilon))$ bit operations, where $\mathcal F(b)=\tilde O(b)$ is the cost of a $b$-bit floating-point operation, and the randomized algorithms of Banks, Garza-Vargas, Kulkarni and Srivastava (arXiv:1912.08805; $O(T_{MM}(n)\log^2(n/\delta))$ arithmetic operations with $O(\log^4(n/\delta)\log n)$ bits) and Shah (arXiv:2408.09880; $\lg(1/\epsilon)+O(\log n+\log\log(1/\epsilon))$ bits, nearly matrix-multiplication time); applied to $L/(2n^{11})$ with $\epsilon=n^{-12}/2$ these give $\tilde O(n^{\omega})$ bit operations independent of $m$. (ii) Solver-based iteration: Spielman and Teng (arXiv:cs/0607105, Theorem 7.2) compute, with probability at least $1-p$, a vector $v\perp\mathbf 1$ with $v^{\top}Lv/v^{\top}v\le(1+\epsilon)\lambda_2(L)$ in $O(m\log^{c}m\log(1/p)\log(1/\epsilon)/\epsilon)$ time by inverse power iteration; Lanczos with a random start (Kuczyński and Woźniakowski) needs only $O(\log(n/\epsilon)/\sqrt{\epsilon})$ Krylov steps in exact arithmetic, so with a nearly-linear-time solver this route costs roughly $\tilde O(m\sqrt{n\lambda_2(L)})\le\tilde O(m\,n^{6})$, which is nearly linear only when $\lambda_2(L)=\tilde O(1/n)$ and is polynomially worse than $\tilde O(n^{\omega})$ in the worst case. Comparison problem: solve $Mx=b$ for a nonsingular $n\times n$ integer matrix $M$ with $n^{O(1)}$ entries and $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ condition number to $n^{-O(1)}$ normwise error, with comparison points $O(n^{\omega})$ for dense $M$ and $\tilde O(n^{(3\omega-4)/(\omega-1)})=O(n^{2.2716})$ for $\tilde O(n)$ nonzeros (Nie, arXiv:2111.05553).

The problem is solved by either (a) reductions, in one or both directions, between $n^{-1}$-accurate $\lambda_2(L)$ estimation for the above graph class and the comparison problem that preserve dimension, number of nonzeros, and $O(\log n)$-bit entries up to polylogarithmic factors (so that the two bit complexities agree up to $\mathrm{polylog}(n)$ factors, in the style of the Kyng and Zhang reductions between structured and general linear systems), or (b) a polynomial separation: an algorithm computing $\tilde\lambda$ in $O(n^{\omega-\delta})$ bit operations for dense graphs, or $O(m^{1+o(1)}\,\mathrm{poly}(\log n))$ for all $m$, for some constant $\delta>0$, or a conditional lower bound showing that such an algorithm would imply a comparably fast algorithm for the comparison problem. A solution must state whether it returns only $\tilde\lambda$ or also a vector $v$ with $v^{\top}Lv/v^{\top}v\le\lambda_2(L)+n^{-1}$, since the two tasks may have different complexity.

literature.description: Proves gap-free bounds for Krylov methods with a random start, in particular that the Lanczos algorithm's probabilistic relative failure decays as $\sqrt{n}e^{-(2k-1)\sqrt{\epsilon}}$ after $k$ matrix-vector products, which gives the $O(\log(n/\epsilon)/\sqrt{\epsilon})$ solve count for solver-based extreme-eigenvalue estimation.
literature.title: Estimating the Largest Eigenvalue by the Power and Lanczos Algorithms with a Random Start

literature.description: Gives the expected $O(m\log^{c}n\log(1/\epsilon))$ SDD solver and, via inverse power iteration (Theorem 7.2), computes with probability at least $1-p$ an $\epsilon$-approximate Fiedler vector (Rayleigh quotient at most $(1+\epsilon)\lambda_2(A)$) in $O(m\log^{c}m\log(1/p)\log(1/\epsilon)/\epsilon)$ time, which is the structure-exploiting baseline for $\lambda_2(L)$.
literature.title: Nearly-Linear Time Algorithms for Preconditioning and Solving Symmetric, Diagonally Dominant Linear Systems

literature.description: Shows that for 2-commodity matrices and other graph-structured classes, solving systems with $s$ nonzeros in $\tilde O(s^{a})$ time is equivalent to solving all linear systems with polynomially bounded integer entries in $\tilde O(s^{a})$ time, providing the sparsity-preserving reduction template that a reduction for $\lambda_2(L)$ would need to follow.
literature.title: Hardness Results for Structured Linear Systems

literature.description: Proves that any randomized algorithm approximating the top-$r$ eigenspace of a symmetric $d\times d$ matrix with normalized gap $\mathrm{gap}$ needs $\Omega(r\log d/\sqrt{\mathrm{gap}})$ matrix-vector queries, matching block-Krylov upper bounds, an unconditional lower bound only in the query model rather than in bit complexity.
literature.title: Tight Query Complexity Lower Bounds for PCA via Finite Sample Deformed Wigner Law

literature.description: Shows that for polynomial accuracy $\Theta(d)$ matrix-vector oracle calls are necessary and sufficient, even for randomized algorithms, for both least-squares regression and top-eigenvector approximation, so any polynomial separation for $\lambda_2(L)$ must exploit explicit access to the graph rather than black-box matrix-vector products.
literature.title: The Gradient Complexity of Linear Regression

literature.description: Gives a randomized algorithm that diagonalizes any $n\times n$ complex matrix to backward error $\delta$ in $O(T_{MM}(n)\log^2(n/\delta))$ arithmetic operations using $O(\log^4(n/\delta)\log n)$ bits of precision, establishing the structure-oblivious nearly matrix-multiplication-time baseline for all eigenvalues.
literature.title: Pseudospectral Shattering, the Sign Function, and Diagonalization in Nearly Matrix Multiplication Time

literature.description: Solves sparse polynomially conditioned linear systems to $1/\mathrm{poly}(n)$ error in $\tilde O(n^{(3\omega-4)/(\omega-1)})=O(n^{2.2716})$ time, the current sparse comparison point for the general integer systems this record contrasts with.
literature.title: Matrix Anti-Concentration Inequalities with Applications

literature.description: Gives a randomized Hermitian diagonalization algorithm in nearly matrix-multiplication time that needs only $\lg(1/\epsilon)+O(\log n+\log\log(1/\epsilon))$ bits of precision, sharpening the finite-precision dense baseline for computing all eigenvalues of $L$.
literature.title: Fast Hermitian Diagonalization with Nearly Optimal Precision

literature.description: Deterministically computes all eigenvalues of a Hermitian matrix to additive error $\epsilon$ in $O(n^{\omega}\mathcal F(\log(n/\epsilon))+n^2\,\mathrm{polylog}(n/\epsilon))$ bit operations and includes spectral-gap computation as a subroutine, giving the dense $\tilde O(n^{\omega})$ bit-complexity baseline for $n^{-1}$-accurate $\lambda_2(L)$.
literature.title: Deterministic Complexity Analysis of Hermitian Eigenproblems

problems.verificationNotes: Fetched all three prior links: arXiv:2410.21550 (Sobczyk) and arXiv:1705.02944 (Kyng–Zhang) are the claimed papers and were kept with sharpened descriptions; arXiv:1512.01892 (Kyng–Lee–Peng–Sachdeva–Spielman, Sparsified Cholesky for connection Laplacians) was checked and removed because its abstract and contribution concern solvers for connection Laplacians, not eigenvalue estimation, and the prior description ('inverse methods approximate small Laplacian eigenvalues using a logarithmic number of linear solves') could not be located in it. Replaced it with the primary source actually establishing the solver-based baseline, Spielman–Teng arXiv:cs/0607105 (Definition 7.1 and Theorem 7.2, ApproxFiedler, verified in the full text), and added the gap-free Lanczos bound of Kuczyński–Woźniakowski (DOI 10.1137/0613066), the dense finite-precision eigensolver baselines (Banks–Garza-Vargas–Kulkarni–Srivastava arXiv:1912.08805, Shah arXiv:2408.09880), the sparse general-system comparison point (Nie arXiv:2111.05553, which is the catalog's benchmark link; the earlier Peng–Vempala bound $O(n^{2.331645})$ at arXiv:2007.10254 was also fetched), and the matrix-vector query lower bounds (arXiv:1804.01221, arXiv:1911.02212). The formulation now states the scale ($\lambda_2(L)\ge 8/n^2$, $\|L\|\le 2n^{11}$, relative accuracy down to $n^{-12}/2$), the success probability, the bit-complexity model, both baselines with their sources, and the concrete criteria for reductions or separation. Searches through 2026-09-20 (arXiv listings, STOC 2026 and FOCS 2026 accepted-paper lists, SODA/ITCS 2026 queries) found no result giving a sparsity-preserving reduction or a polynomial separation between $n^{-1}$-accurate $\lambda_2$ of unnormalized integer-weighted Laplacians and general polynomially conditioned integer systems; the closest 2025 item, arXiv:2508.19898 (distributed sparsest cut via eigenvalue estimation), concerns normalized Laplacians in the CONGEST model and does not address this record. Status remains open. Title changed only to wrap $\lambda_2(L)$ in inline math delimiters; source statement unchanged.

resolutionAudit.assessment: Upper bounds are well documented in two regimes: structure-oblivious dense Hermitian eigensolvers (deterministic $O(n^{\omega}\mathcal F(\log(n/\epsilon))+n^2\,\mathrm{polylog}(n/\epsilon))$ bit operations, Sobczyk; randomized nearly matrix-multiplication time with $\mathrm{polylog}$ or $\log(1/\epsilon)+O(\log n)$ bits, BGVKS and Shah) and solver-based inverse/Krylov iteration whose cost scales with the relative accuracy $1/(n\lambda_2(L))$ (Spielman–Teng Theorem 7.2, Kuczyński–Woźniakowski). Lower bounds exist only in the matrix-vector query model ($\Theta(d)$ queries for polynomial accuracy, Braverman et al.; gap-dependent bounds, Simchowitz et al.). No primary source found through 2026-09-20 gives a reduction preserving sparsity and $O(\log n)$-bit entries between $n^{-1}$-accurate $\lambda_2$ of unnormalized integer-weighted Laplacians and general polynomially conditioned integer systems, nor a conditional polynomial separation; the Kyng–Zhang hardness framework covers 2-commodity and other graph-structured linear systems but not eigenvalue problems for Laplacians. Confidence is medium because the negative finding rests on keyword searches of arXiv and 2026 conference lists rather than an exhaustive review.

resolutionAudit.remainingGap: A reduction in either direction, preserving dimension, number of nonzeros, and $O(\log n)$-bit entries up to polylogarithmic factors, between $n^{-1}$-additive estimation of $\lambda_2(L)$ for connected integer-weighted (weights in $[1,n^{10}]$) undirected Laplacians and solving polynomially conditioned general integer systems to $1/\mathrm{poly}(n)$ error; or an algorithm for $\lambda_2(L)$ beating $\tilde O(n^{\omega})$ bit operations on dense graphs (ideally $m^{1+o(1)}$ for all $m$); or a conditional lower bound.
